title: Heart valve replacement
what: The surgeon replaces a damaged heart valve with an artificial one. It is usually open surgery. Sometimes the valve is placed through a blood vessel without opening the chest.
why: When a valve is badly narrowed or does not close, and the heart cannot cope.
duration: surgery usually takes 3 to 5 hours, with 7 to 14 days in hospital; less when placed through a vessel
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Kidney or lung disease, or diabetes
Any bad teeth. They are treated before surgery
If you plan a pregnancy. This matters for the choice of valve

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, a heart ultrasound, and a coronary angiogram or CT. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: Your teeth usually need treatment before surgery to prevent infection.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Arrange in advance who will help you at home for the first weeks.

bring: A note from your dentist, if asked
Documents and a list of your medicines
Things for a 1 to 2 week hospital stay
steps: You change, and IV lines are placed
The anesthetist gives anesthesia, and you fall asleep
In open surgery, the heart is connected to a heart-lung machine
The surgeon removes the diseased valve and sews in a new one
The heart is restarted, the breastbone is closed, and the wound is stitched
You wake up in intensive care
feel: Chest pain from the cut. You will get painkillers
A mechanical valve can sometimes be heard as a soft click. This is normal
after: You start getting up in the first days
For a few weeks, protect the breastbone: no heavy lifting or pushing up with your arms
With a mechanical valve, blood thinners are needed for life, with regular blood tests
Before dental work and other procedures, tell the doctor you have an artificial valve
red_flags: Chest pain or severe shortness of breath: call emergency services
Sudden weakness of an arm or leg, or trouble speaking: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) with no clear cause
Bleeding or bruising for no reason, if you take blood thinners

faq.q: Which valve is better, mechanical or tissue?
faq.a: A mechanical valve lasts longer, but you need blood thinners for life. A tissue valve does not need them, but can wear out. You choose with your surgeon.

faq.q: Why treat my teeth before surgery?
faq.a: Infection from the teeth can reach the new valve. So teeth are treated in advance.

reminders.text: Heart valve surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, things, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
